title: Compute voltage-dependent amplitude-frequency curves
action: Implement the dimensionless nonlinear governing equations for a symmetric cross-ply [PZT5/0/90/0/90/0/PZT5] laminated piezoelectric plate using Timoshenko-Mindlin kinematics and orthotropic piezoelectric constitutive relations. Apply a one-term Galerkin approximation to reduce the PDEs to an ODE, then use the method of harmonic balance to obtain the dimensionless nonlinear frequency ratio ω/ω₀ as a function of dimensionless amplitude W/h. Compute the curves for the applied voltage cases V = 0 V, +200 V, +400 V, −200 V, −400 V. Write the computed (amplitude_ratio, frequency_ratio, voltage) triples to voltage_vs_frequency.csv.
description: CSV file containing the nonlinear amplitude-frequency response data for the [PZT5/0/90/0/90/0/PZT5] plate at five different applied voltages. This reproduces the paper's main result on the effect of piezoelectric actuation on vibration frequency.
output_schema: CSV with columns: amplitude_ratio (float, dimensionless amplitude W/h), frequency_ratio (float, dimensionless nonlinear frequency ω/ω₀), voltage (integer, applied voltage in V). One row per computed datapoint.

title: Compute location-dependent amplitude-frequency curves
action: Using the same model and solution methodology, compute the amplitude-frequency curves for three lamination schemes under zero applied voltage: [0/90/PZT5/0/PZT5/90/0] (middle), [0/PZT5/90/0/90/PZT5/0] (inner), [PZT5/0/90/0/90/0/PZT5] (top_bottom). Write the computed (amplitude_ratio, frequency_ratio, lamination_case) triples to location_vs_frequency.csv.
description: CSV file comparing the amplitude-frequency response for three different placements of piezoelectric layers within the laminate. This quantifies the effect of piezoelectric layer location on vibration frequency.
output_schema: CSV with columns: amplitude_ratio (float, dimensionless amplitude W/h), frequency_ratio (float, dimensionless nonlinear frequency ω/ω₀), lamination_case (string, one of 'top_bottom', 'middle', 'inner'). One row per computed datapoint.
